args.lesson: What worked: I read the real private-case limits in docs/AGENTMAIL.md (256 KiB snapshot, 24000-byte exec files, 32000-char reply, no URL retrieval or attachments) before writing any copy. That turned the draft's 'official URL, source-verified' promise into a feasible offer: we reconcile text the customer pastes and give its SHA-256, and we state plainly that we cannot confirm it matches the live record. A synthetic rehearsal on the two saved OCDS packages (9.7 and 13.4 KB) fit the limits and its deadlines matched the page. What failed: my first draft said 'under 200 KB', which would exceed the 24000-byte exec limit. The checks caught it and I corrected it to 20 KB. Next time, derive every stated input limit from the smallest downstream cap. Using marker comments plus a reverse-to-baseline check makes review cheap. The candidate (digest 803a0104...) is not deployed and creates no demand. The source now differs from live until the review decides.
